title: Telemetry-driven INT8 calibrator feedback loop and microkernel operator
creator: Diego Morales
description:
Goal:
Build an end-to-end INT8 calibration service that closes the loop between offline calibration profiles (activation-aware scaling), runtime telemetry, and microkernel selection so we can safely deploy activation-preserving quantized variants at scale. This ticket implements the operator that applies per-model calibrator outputs, attaches runtime quality monitoring hooks, and orchestrates fallback to higher-precision kernels when regressions are detected.

Background:
- We have existing calibration tooling that computes per-channel/per-layer scaling factors for SmoothQuant-style activation-aware INT8 conversion, but deployments require tighter runtime validation and automatic mitigation.
- Production traces show edge-case activation distributions (prefix-heavy kv-cache, long-chat histories) that cause token-level degradation for some models after quantization. Manual rollbacks are slow.

Scope / Deliverables:
1) Calibrator feedback loop service: API that ingests nightly eval metrics (accuracy deltas, perplexity, sample-level diffs), correlates them with model/version/quant-profile, and outputs a confidence score plus remediation suggestion (recalibrate / adjust scale / revert kernel).
2) Microkernel operator: runtime component that consumes the calibrator output and performs safe kernel swaps per-layer or per-op group. Supports hot-switching to fallback FP16/FP32 kernels without dropping active requests (graceful degrade).
3) Runtime hooks for telemetry: lightweight sampling that records activation histograms, quantization mismatch counters, and per-request quality markers (for labeled eval prompts).
4) CI/eval integration: pipeline job that runs new quant profiles against the eval suite, pushes metrics to the calibrator service, and gates deployment via confidence thresholds.

Design notes:
- Confidence score uses weighted signals: eval accuracy regression (50%), activation-distribution divergence (25%), production error rate uptick (15%), tail-latency anomalies (10%).
- Operator chooses between three actions: NOOP, HOTPATCH (adjust microkernel or scale param), ROLLBACK (switch to safe kernel variant).
- Hotpatch must be idempotent and annotated in trace/span for audit.
- Fallback kernel set is prioritized by cost/latency impact: INT8-optimized -> mixed-precision (FP16 fused ops) -> FP32 reference.
- Telemetry sampling at 0.5% by default, increased to 2% for canary cohorts.

Acceptance criteria:
- Calibrator service accepts nightly-eval payloads and returns a confidence score within 2s for a 1000-sample batch.
- Operator can hotpatch a per-layer kernel without dropping in-flight requests in >=95% of trials in staging.
- CI job blocks merge if confidence < 0.85 and marks the release candidate for manual review.
- End-to-end run on two internal models (llama-13b variant, redwood-chat-7b) shows no more than 0.5% median accuracy regression post-deploy.

Tasks (initial):
- [ ] API schema and protobuf for calibrator ingestion (Diego)
- [ ] Service skeleton + simple rule-based scorer (Ava)
- [ ] Microkernel operator prototype (Jacob)
- [ ] Telemetry sampling instrumentation and activation histogram code (Priya)
- [ ] CI job and gating automation (Sana)
- [ ] Nightly eval dashboard panels and alerts (Observability team)

Dependencies:
["ENG-5421", "ENG-98200"] , note: ENG-5421 contains smoothquant-int8 kernel integration work we rely on for baseline kernels.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Telemetry volume could increase cost and RD storage. Mitigation: sampling and adaptive rate limiting; store histogram aggregates rather than raw tensors.
- Risk: Hotpatching introduces state mismatch. Mitigation: operator enforces versioned kernel ABI and runs a local dry-run verification on a sampled batch before flipping.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge calibrator service behind feature flag; run in read-only mode for 2 weeks.
2) Enable operator in staging with canary cohort (5% traffic) for one model.
3) Expand to additional models and increase sampling; tune thresholds.
4) Full rollout when confidence >0.9 for 30 days or manual sign-off.
